content: A night owl refers to an individual who habitually stays awake until late at night. Typically, night owls remain awake past midnight, with some extreme cases staying up until 5:00 or 6:00 in the morning. For some, this behavior is a matter of personal preference or a habitual pattern, while others may stay awake late due to occupational demands, such as working night shifts. Individuals who experience significant difficulty in aligning their sleep and wake cycles with conventional schedules may suffer from a condition known as delayed sleep phase syndrome (DSPS). Additionally, a preference for the nighttime or a darker environment is referred to as nyctophilia or scotophilia. The counterpart to a night owl is an early bird, also known as a lark, which describes someone who tends to go to bed early and wake up early. In some cultures, early risers are referred to as A-people, while those who stay up late are called B-people. Researchers studying sleep patterns often use the terms morningness and eveningness to describe these tendencies. Notable individuals who have been identified as night owls include Winston Churchill, Bill Clinton, Glenn Gould, Elvis Presley, Marcel Proust, and J.R.R. Tolkien.
